Philosophy Connection

Weekly theme: Winning Moments. A low block does not break because we shoot harder, it breaks because we move the ball, and the block, until a real window opens. Tonight is about telling the difference between a shooting window and a moving window, and making the pass that creates the next one.

Session Objectives
  • Recognize a shooting window versus a moving window before the shot, based on defender distance and a clear lane to goal (Passive and Shifting, Half Pressure, Scrimmage)
  • Move the block with a switch of play and combine to open the lane instead of shooting into traffic (Low Block Switch drills, Scrimmage)
  • Choose between 7 and 2 based on where 7's defender steps, decided before the ball arrives (Passive and Shifting, Half Pressure)
  • Screen with 9 and 10: use the body to keep defenders from stepping out to the shooter (Passive and Shifting)
  • Recycle and restart the attack when neither 7 nor 2 is on, without forcing the shot (Half Pressure, Scrimmage)

Activity 2 of 6  ·  Activation
Square Passing
Four Variations  ·  Movement After the Pass  ·  15 minutes
Format
Squares, same set-up as W13S01
Variations
4
Focus
Body shape + next action
Duration
15 min
V1 Back Foot · V2 3rd Man · V3 1-2 Combo · V4 Diagonal
Objective Sharpen the passing and movement that tonight's patterns depend on. The first touch sets up the next action, and the movement after the pass is part of the pass. The Cruyff turn stays deferred to a B1 session.
Variations
1 · Back FootReceive on the back foot with the body already opening to the next target.
2 · 3rd ManThe pass is made to set up the player who is not yet involved.
3 · 1-2 ComboPass, move, and receive the return in a new position.
4 · DiagonalDiagonal pass through the square, then move to a new support position.
Coaching Points
  • Where is your body pointing when the ball arrives?
  • After you pass, where are you going and why?
  • Does your first touch set up the next pass, or just stop the ball?
Activity 3 of 6  ·  Block Training
Low Block Switch: No Defense
Scripted Pattern  ·  Both Directions  ·  8 minutes
Players
11, 8, 6, 7 working, 3 and 2 in line
GK
Live in goal
Defense
None
Duration
8 min
Switch Pattern: 11 to 8, 8 to 6, 6 to 7 to Finish
Objective Learn the shape of the pattern before it has to survive a defense. Kept short on purpose: every rep is the same pass sequence, so the decisions start in the next activity.

Pattern

11 dribbles and plays to 8, who has dropped. 8 switches to 6, who has also dropped. 6 plays to 7, who checks in to receive and shoots. 3 and 2 wait behind 11 and 7 and rotate in.

Both Directions

Run the pattern left to right, then mirror it right to left. Rotations: 11 and 7, 8 and 6, 9 and 10, 2 and 3.

Coaching Points
  • 8 and 6: are you dropping to receive with your body already open to the next pass?
  • 6: is your pass weighted for 7 to shoot on the first touch?
  • 7: when did you start your movement, before or after 6 had the ball?
Activity 4 of 6  ·  Block Training
Low Block Switch: Passive and Shifting
The 7 / 2 Decision  ·  9 and 10 Screen  ·  17 minutes
Attack
11, 8, 6, 7, 9, 10, 2, 3
Defense
6 + GK, shift only
Tackling
No ball wins
Duration
17 min
Option 1: 6 Plays 7, 9 and 10 Screen, 8 Is the Outlet
Option 2: 7 Checks In to Pull a Defender, 2 Arrives Late
Objective Put a decision into the pattern. The defenders shift ball-side with each pass, so the switch actually moves the block. 6 reads 7's defender, 7 and 2 attack the space it leaves, and the shot only happens when the window is real.

Defense

6 defenders and the GK. They slide ball-side with every pass but do not tackle or win the ball. The shift is what makes the switch worth playing.

9 and 10 Screen

Hold positions in the box and angle the body to keep the two nearest defenders from stepping out to 7 or 2. If a defender steps out anyway, the screener peels to the vacated space for the rebound or cutback.

Triggers: 6 Reads 7's Defender When the Ball Arrives
Play 7The defender stays off 7 and the lane is clear of bodies. 7 receives and shoots.
Play 2The defender steps to 7, or a body is in the lane. 7 checks in to pull the defender. 2 starts the run when 7 checks in, not when the ball is played, and arrives late into the space 7 left.
RecycleNeither is on. 6 plays back to 8 or across to 3, and the ball restarts on the other side.
Coaching Points
  • 6: did 7's defender step to him before the ball arrived?
  • 7: what did you see when you checked in?
  • 2: did your run start when 7 checked in, or when the ball was played?
  • 9 and 10: which defender are you keeping out of the lane?
  • Was that a shooting window or a moving window?
Activity 5 of 6  ·  Block Training
Low Block Switch: Half Pressure
Defense Can Win the Ball  ·  Clock Is Live  ·  12 minutes
Attack
Same 8 players, same roles
Defense
6 + GK at about half intensity
Clock
30 seconds
Duration
12 min
Same Options: 7 Checks In, 2 Arrives Late, 8 Is the Outlet
Objective Same options, now with a defense that can win the ball and a scoreboard that rewards patience. A shot into traffic burns the clock, so the move-it option starts to look better than the traffic shot.

Scoring

Attack: a goal after a switch is worth 2, a goal without a switch is worth 1. Defense: 1 point for every 30 seconds they hold the low block.

Clock and Restarts

The clock starts on the first pass and resets after a goal. A blocked shot, a won ball, or a ball out all restart the attack from 11 with the clock still running. Defense pays nothing for a blocked shot, but the time spent is theirs.

Coaching Points
  • What did you see before you shot?
  • Was that a shooting window or a moving window?
  • Did the shift of play move the block, or did the defense just slide back?
  • When neither 7 nor 2 was on, who was your recycle?
Activity 6 of 6  ·  Scrimmage
Low Block Scrimmage
8v6 + GK  ·  Half Field  ·  Defenders Rotate  ·  23 minutes
Format
8v6 + GK
Field
Half field
Scoring
Same as Activity 5
Duration
23 min
Objective Take it live. No scripted pattern, no assigned runs, just the triggers and the clock. The attack has to find its own window against a block that is trying to hold.

Rules

Same scoring and 30-second clock as Activity 5. Defenders rotate out every 5 to 6 minutes so every group attacks and defends.

Restarts

When the defense wins the ball, the attack restarts from the back with the clock still running. No counter-attack, the defense is practicing holding the block.

Coaching Points
  • What told you the window was open before you shot?
  • Who moved the block last, and how?
  • Which of your triggers showed up without being asked?
